slides.title: Encapsulation with @property Decorator
slides.prompt: The @property decorator allows you to define getter, setter, and deleter methods for a class attribute, giving you control over attribute access and validation while maintaining a clean syntax.

slides.title: Protected Attribute Naming Convention
slides.prompt: What is the standard Python naming convention to signal that an attribute is intended for internal/protected use?

slides.title: Property Setter Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the decorator name used to define a setter method for a property named 'age'.

slides.title: Name Mangling in Python
slides.prompt: What happens when you name an attribute with double leading underscores (e.g., __password) inside a class?
options: Python triggers name mangling by rewriting the attribute name as _ClassName__password to prevent subclass collisions
Python turns the attribute into a read-only constant
Python throws an AttributeError if accessed outside the class file
Python automatically encrypts the attribute's value in RAM
slides.correctAnswer: Python triggers name mangling by rewriting the attribute name as _ClassName__password to prevent subclass collisions

slides.title: Property Deleter Decorator
slides.prompt: Fill in the decorator used to handle attribute deletion via the 'del' statement.

slides.title: Read-Only Properties
slides.prompt: How do you create a read-only property in a Python class?
options: Define a method with the @property decorator but do NOT define a corresponding .setter method
Set the attribute value using const inside __init__
Use double trailing underscores on the property method name
slides.correctAnswer: Define a method with the @property decorator but do NOT define a corresponding .setter method
